sentences.text: None appears for respondent No.2.

This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed to invoke the extra ordinary jurisdiction of
this Court and to quash the proceeding of Complaint Case No.10412/2008 pending before the
Special Judge (under the Municipality Act), Jabalpur for offences punishable under Sections 7 and
16 (1) (a) (i) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

Briefly stated the prosecution story is that respondent No.2/B.S. Jamod, the Food Inspector of
Jabalpur filed a complaint case before the Court of Special Magistrate (under the Municipal Act)
Jabalpur for offence under Sections 7 and 16 (1) (a) (i) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration
Act, 1954 read with Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules.

It is contented that the Food Inspector taken a sample from one Baliram Pandey who was carrying
milk in Autorickshaw bearing Registration No.M.P.-20-LA-1120.

The driver/Baliram Pandey
informed the inspector that the milk belongs to the petitioner.

Three samples of the milk were seized
and one sample was sent to State Food Laboratory, Bhopal for examination.

Another sample was
sent to the Public Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Bhopal while the third sample was deposited with
the Local Heath Authority, Mandla.
It is contented that the report of sample which was sent for analysis was received with report dated
04/06/2008.
It is found that the sample of milk is adulterated.

However, compliance of Section
13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was not made and no notice was given to the
petitioner, therefore, the petitioner was deprived of his rights.

The petitioner, therefore, claimed that as there is violation of the provisions envisaged, the
complaint against the petitioner deserves to be quashed.
Counsel for the respondent/State opposed the contentions.

Sub Section 2 of Section 13 of Prevention
of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 provides that, when the report of the analysis shows that the article
of food is adulterated and a prosecution has been instituted, Sub Section 2 requires its Local
(Health) Authority to send a copy of the report to the accused and to intimate to him that he may
make an application to the Court to get the second part of the sample analyzed by the Central Food

Laboratory.
This provision is mandatory and violation thereof will entitle the accused to acquittal.

The object of
this Sub Section2 is to afford an opportunity to the accused to get the sample analyzed, if he so
desires to examine the second sample by the Central Food Laboratory, the certificate shall be final
and conclusive.

Thus, the Sub Section amount at fair play and if the accused feels that the sample is
not properly or accurately analyzed or some other samples that one taken from the accused was
analyzed or that the conclusion arrived by the public analyst were erroneous

, he may get the other
part of the sample kept by the local (health) authority analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory
through the Court.

It not only gives the person from whom the sample is taken, a copy of the analyst
report but also through his to his right to have the sample analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory
by making an application to the Court within a fixed time.

Counsel for the petitioner placed reliance in the case of Ravindra Chopade Vs. State of M.P. reported
as 2013(1) Mpwn 118, in which it is held that accused was deprived of valuable right to get the
sample analyzed before expiry date of the product- proceedings quashed.

Counsel for the petitioner also placed reliance on Prahlad Gattani & others Vs. State of M.P.
reported as 2012(4) Mpht 358, in which it is held that, Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954,
Sections 7/16 and 13- Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, Rule 32(b) (2) (v)- Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 482- Delay in forwarding notice under Section 13(2) of the Act
along with copy of report of Public Analyst-The sample of Ketch, drawn by the Food Inspector was
forwarded for analysis to Public Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Bhopal-

The report dated
23/02/2010 indicated that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed, despite
declaration made on the label that Ketchup was "best before 6 months" from January, 2010, the
date of its manufacture-

Notice under Section 13(2) of the Act along with copy of the report of the
Public Analyst was forwarded to petitioner No.1/accused on 29/07/2011, i.e., nearly a year after the
expiry of the shelf life of the sample- Held, petitioners/accused were deprived of their right to get
the sample re-analyzed by Central Food Laboratory a

s contemplated under Section 13(2) of the Act causing serious prejudice to them resulting in failure of justice- Petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. allowed and proceedings of the Criminal Case quashed.
In the present case, no document has been produced by the complainant before the Court which shows that mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the Act was complied with.

Although, adulteration of food is a menace to public health and the Act has been enacted with an aim of eradicating that antisocial evil and ensuring purity in the articles of food yet, the authority concerned are duty bound to ensure that the valuable right conferred by Section 13(2) of the Act is not defeated due to inefficiency and ineptitude.
For the reasons mentioned above, the petition is allowed.

Proceeding in Complaint Case No.10412/2008 pending before the Special Judge under the Municipality Act, Jabalpur for offences punishable under Sections 7 and 16 (1) (a) (i) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is hereby quashed.
